payload.report: The patient's enlarging right anterior thigh mass appears with hip flexion and disappears on extension, a hallmark of mechanical fascial etiology. Dynamic ultrasound and MRI confirm focal fascial bulging with rectus femoris convexity during hip flexion and no underlying mass, directly supporting a muscle hernia or fascial defect. Plain radiography shows no osseous abnormality, further excluding tumor or inflammatory causes. The absence of a detectable mass on imaging and lack of skin changes or tenderness refute soft tissue tumor and inflammatory/infectious mass. With strong imaging and clinical convergence and a confidence of 0.95, the diagnosis is sufficiently established as muscle hernia/fascial defect, requiring no further refinement.
